candidate_targets: emotional reactions to negative self-referential content
contraindications: Uncertain; no explicit contraindications mentioned in the text
original_extraction.evidence_text:
Bring an unpleasant image to mind and notice how it’s affecting you. Now imagine there’s a small
television screen across the room from you. Place your image on the television screen. Play around
with the image: flip it upside down; turn it on its side; spin it around and around; stre-e-e-etch it
sideways. If it’s a moving ‘video clip’, play it in slow motion. Then play it backwards in slow
motion. Then play it forwards at double speed; then reverse it at double speed. Turn the colour
down, so it’s all in black-and-white. Turn the colour and brightness up until it’s ridiculously lurid
(so the people have bright orange skin and the clouds are hot pink). The idea is not to get rid of this
image but to see it for what it is: a harmless picture. You may need to do this for anything from ten
seconds to two minutes, until you really defuse it. If at the end of two minutes it’s still bothering
you, then try the next technique.

---

Keeping that image on the television screen, add a humorous subtitle or voice-over to it, such as
“The Ultimate Disaster! premieres on Channel 4, Friday, 7.30pm’ or ‘Now showing at a movie
theatre near you: / Got Rejected By My Lover!” If this image is linked to a story that you’ve already
named, then use that name on the subtitle or voice-over. For example, an image of you failing might
be subtitled: ‘The “Failure” Story’. If it’s still bothering you at the end of another 30 seconds, try
the next technique.

---

Keeping that image on the television screen, add a musical soundtrack of your choice. Experiment
with a few different soundtracks: jazz, hip-hop, classical, rock or your favourite movie themes. If
the image is still bothering you, try the next technique.
generation_rules: Place the unpleasant image on an imagined television screen
Manipulate the image by changing orientation, speed, and color
Add humorous subtitles or voice-overs related to the image
Add a musical soundtrack of choice to the image
pause_rules: Pause after each manipulation step to assess emotional impact and distress level
original_extraction.psychological_function: Reduces emotional intensity and distress associated with unpleasant mental images by changing their sensory qualities and contextual framing
repetition_rules: Continue image manipulation for 10 seconds to 2 minutes until defusion occurs
If distress persists, add subtitles/voice-overs for 30 seconds
If distress still persists, add musical soundtrack and experiment with different genres
original_extraction.therapeutic_function: Defusion from distressing mental images by altering perception and emotional impact through imaginative manipulation
voice_rules: Use humorous or ironic subtitles or voice-overs to reframe the image contextually
